**Release strategy: cut 1.0 now (controlled pilot), 1.1 = the epic**

What: Release strategy decided (supersedes the earlier hybrid M1+M2 cut).
Decision: merge feature/v2.0.0 -> main and tag 1.0 NOW, adopted by a CONTROLLED PILOT (own repos / Sinergia). Because the environment is controlled, auto-update-safety does NOT block 1.0 — upgrade risk is self-owned, closed in 1.1. All new work (M2-M8) goes to the 1.1 line.
1.0 minimal-honest set: merge+tag 1.0; REQUIRED KNOWN-LIMITATIONS in release notes (upgrade has no rollback = not for external adopters, reviewer flow-guarantees inert #317, phantom backends unimplemented, first-install manual package.json step); cheap+recommended 1-liners: trim phantom allow-list (G4), ADR for 3-axis (G3).
1.1 line = the epic M2-M8, chained PRs, order M2->M3->M4->M5->M8->M6->M7.
HARD GATE before opening to EXTERNAL adoption: auto-update-safety (M4 subset — rollback/atomic-write U4, clobber asymmetry U3, corrupt-file lockout U6) must land before any uncontrolled third party runs brain:upgrade. That's the pilot->open-product boundary.
Numbering: public tag starts at 1.0; next line is 1.1 (NOT 2.1 — v2.0.0 was the internal branch name). One scheme only.
Global sequence: [trim G4 + KNOWN-LIMITATIONS] -> merge v2->main + tag 1.0 -> 1.1(M2..M8) -> [gate: auto-update-safety] -> external adopters.
User's key insight/fear: installation. Resolved by splitting it — distribution (how brain gets IN, defer to 1.1) vs auto-update (how it UPGRADES, the mortal-risk axis, gated for external).
Docs: docs/inbox/brain-v2-epic-plan.md. Related: [[architecture/v2-epic-plan]] [[architecture/v2-merge-audit]].
